title: SVO Order and Equative Sentences (Adalah vs Ialah)
subtitle: Forming basic sentences without linking verbs and using optional copular markers correctly
keyPoint: Indonesian follows Subject-Verb-Object word order and typically requires no linking verb (like 'to be') between subjects and their descriptions or identities.

cells: Subject + Noun directly (I am a teacher)
Used before noun phrases in formal or definitional statements
Used interchangeably with 'adalah' to define identity

useCases.label: Describing with Adjectives
useCases.example: Rumah ini sangat besar.

useCases.label: Stating Professions Directly
useCases.example: Ayah saya dokter.

useCases.label: Formal Definitions with Adalah
useCases.example: Pancasila adalah dasar negara.

examples.en: Mereka bahagia hari ini.
Budi membaca buku di kamar.
Ibu saya adalah guru bahasa Indonesia.
Masalah utama ialah kurangnya waktu.
Mobil itu baru dan cepat.

mistakes.note: Never use 'adalah' before an adjective. Only place adjectives directly after the subject.
'Ada' indicates presence or possession (there is / to exist), not identity.
Indonesian strictly follows SVO word order in active sentences.

quiz.question: Choose the natural way to say: 'My younger sibling is smart.'
quiz.explanation: 'Pintar' is an adjective, so no copula should be used between the subject and the predicate.

quiz.question: Complete the formal definition: 'Indonesia ___ negara kepulauan.'
quiz.explanation: 'Adalah' functions as the formal copula before noun phrases in definitions.

quiz.question: How do you say: 'We are students.'
quiz.explanation: In standard Indonesian, the subject simply joins the noun predicate directly without any linking verb.

quiz.question: Which sentence incorrectly uses a linking word?
quiz.explanation: 'Ramah' (friendly) is an adjective, making 'adalah' grammatically incorrect here.

tip: If the word following the subject describes a feeling, size, or quality (adjective), simply drop the English 'am/is/are' entirely!

title: Negation: Tidak vs Bukan
subtitle: Distinguishing between verb/adjective negation (tidak) and noun/identity negation (bukan)
keyPoint: Use 'tidak' to negate verbs and adjectives, and use 'bukan' to negate nouns, pronouns, and identities.

useCases.label: Negating Actions
useCases.example: Kami tidak pergi ke bioskop.

useCases.label: Negating Qualities
useCases.example: Baju ini tidak mahal.

useCases.label: Negating Nouns / Identities
useCases.example: Dia bukan orang Jepang.

examples.en: Saya tidak tahu jawabannya.
Kopi ini tidak manis.
Ini bukan tas milik Andi.
Mereka tidak mau makan sekarang.
Itu bukan kesalahan Anda.

mistakes.note: 'Lapar' is an adjective, so it must be negated with 'tidak'.
'Guru' is a noun designating a profession, so it requires 'bukan'.
'Buku saya' is a noun phrase, requiring 'bukan' instead of 'tidak'.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'Rumah kami ___ besar, tetapi nyaman.'
quiz.explanation: 'Besar' is an adjective, so it must be negated with 'tidak'.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'Orang itu ___ paman saya.'
quiz.explanation: 'Paman saya' (my uncle) is a noun phrase, requiring 'bukan' to negate identity.

quiz.question: Choose the correct sentence to mean 'I do not understand':
quiz.explanation: 'Mengerti' is a verb, which takes 'tidak'.

quiz.question: Complete the contrast: 'Dia ___ murid, melainkan guru.'
quiz.explanation: Contrasting noun categories ('not a student, but a teacher') requires 'bukan'.

tip: Think of 'bukan' as 'not a / not the' for things and people, while 'tidak' covers doing and feeling!

title: Demonstratives (Ini/Itu) and Definiteness with -nya
subtitle: Using post-nominal determiners and -nya to mark specificity, possession, and definiteness
keyPoint: Demonstratives ('ini' for near, 'itu' for far) always follow the noun they modify, while the suffix '-nya' marks the definite article 'the' or third-person possession.

cells: Marks proximity to speaker (mobil ini = this car)
Marks distance from speaker (gedung itu = that building)

useCases.label: Pointing Close Things (Ini)
useCases.example: Kemeja ini sangat bersih.

useCases.label: Pointing Distant Things (Itu)
useCases.example: Pohon kelapa itu tinggi sekali.

useCases.label: Marking Definiteness (-nya)
useCases.example: Kopinya enak sekali.

examples.en: Kucing ini suka tidur di sofa.
Restoran itu sangat ramai pengunjung.
Mobilnya rusak kemarin malam.
Kunci rumah ini milik siapa?
Harganya terlalu mahal untuk saya.

mistakes.note: Demonstratives must follow the noun they modify in Indonesian, unlike in English.
When adjectives modify a noun, 'itu' goes after the adjective at the end of the noun phrase.
Do not double third-person pronouns; use either 'buku dia' or 'bukunya'.

quiz.question: How do you correctly translate: 'This hotel is comfortable'?
quiz.explanation: In Indonesian, demonstrative adjectives follow the noun: 'Hotel ini'.

quiz.question: Where does 'itu' belong in 'that black cat'?
quiz.explanation: The order is Noun + Adjective + Demonstrative: 'Kucing hitam itu'.

quiz.question: In the sentence 'Makanannya lezat,' what role does '-nya' play?
options: Turns the noun into a question
quiz.explanation: The enclitic '-nya' turns an indefinite noun into a definite one, equivalent to English 'the food'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence to mean 'His bag is new': '___ baru.'
quiz.explanation: '-nya' attaches directly to the possessed noun to denote 'his/her bag'.

tip: Remember the golden word-order rule: Head noun first, then its adjectives, and demonstratives (ini/itu) last!

title: Numeral Classifiers (Kata Penggolong)
subtitle: Pairing numbers with standard counting words like orang, ekor, buah, and lembar
keyPoint: When counting nouns, Indonesian frequently places a specific classifier between the numeral and the noun based on whether the entity is human, animal, inanimate, or flat.

useCases.label: Counting Humans (orang)
useCases.example: Ada lima orang murid di perpustakaan.

useCases.label: Counting Animals (ekor)
useCases.example: Paman membeli empat ekor ayam.

useCases.label: General Objects (buah)
useCases.example: Saya membeli dua buah kursi baru.

examples.en: Dua orang guru datang ke kelas.
Kucing itu melahirkan tiga ekor anak kucing.
Ibu meletakkan sebuah semangka di meja.
Tolong beri saya selembar tisu.
Dia memiliki empat buah sepeda motor.

mistakes.note: 'Ekor' literally means 'tail' and is exclusively for animals, never humans.
Birds and other animals take 'ekor', whereas 'orang' is reserved for humans.
Sheets of paper and thin flat objects use 'lembar' rather than 'buah'.

quiz.question: Which classifier should fill the blank: 'Saya melihat tiga ___ burung di pohon.'?
quiz.explanation: Animals are counted with the classifier 'ekor' (literally 'tail').

quiz.question: How do you say 'a teacher' using the single prefix 'se-'?
quiz.explanation: The prefix 'se-' combines with 'orang' to make 'seorang' for a single human being.

quiz.question: Which phrase correctly expresses 'two sheets of paper'?
quiz.explanation: 'Lembar' is the classifier used for paper, sheets, and thin flat materials.

quiz.question: Which classifier is most appropriate for 'dua ___ mobil'?
quiz.explanation: 'Buah' is the standard classifier for general 3D objects, vehicles, and fruits.

tip: When the quantity is one, 'satu' blends with the classifier into the prefix 'se-' (seorang = a person, seekor = an animal, sebuah = an item).

title: Question Formation and the -kah Interrogative Enclitic
subtitle: Using WH-words in situ vs fronted, and attaching -kah for formal polar questions
keyPoint: Indonesian question words can sit at the front or remain in place (in situ), and the enclitic '-kah' attaches to the focused element in formal yes/no inquiries.

useCases.label: Informal In Situ Questions
useCases.example: Kamu tinggal di mana?

useCases.label: Fronted WH-Questions
useCases.example: Mengapa dia terlambat?

useCases.label: Formal Yes/No with -kah
useCases.example: Bolehkah saya masuk?

examples.en: Apakah Anda sudah makan malam?
Siapa yang memasak makanan ini?
Kapan toko buku itu buka?
Benarkah kabar tentang dia?
Mau beli apa di pasar?

mistakes.note: Use 'apa' for 'what' and 'apakah' for yes/no questions; 'apakah kamu beli?' means 'Are you buying (something)?'.
Do not stack extra unnecessary verbs with location questions.
'-kah' is an attached enclitic and must be written joined without a space.

quiz.question: Which word turns a simple statement into a polite yes/no question?
quiz.explanation: 'Apakah' is placed at the front of a sentence to form a formal yes/no question.

quiz.question: How do you ask 'Where do you work?' naturally in Indonesian?
quiz.explanation: 'Di mana' translates to 'where (at what place)'.

quiz.question: Attach the interrogative particle correctly to 'Boleh' (May/Can):
quiz.explanation: The particle '-kah' must attach directly to the verb or predicate as an enclitic: 'Bolehkah'.

quiz.question: Select the proper question word for 'Who is that person?': '___ orang itu?'
quiz.explanation: 'Siapa' is used when asking about identity or people ('who').

tip: In everyday conversational Indonesian, speakers often drop '-kah' and 'apakah' completely, relying solely on rising intonation at the end of the sentence!

title: Temporal and Aspectual Markers
subtitle: Expressing time and completion using pre-verbal aspect words
keyPoint: Indonesian verbs never conjugate for tense; instead, place aspect markers like sudah, belum, sedang, and akan immediately before the verb.

useCases.label: Completed Action
useCases.example: Budi sudah menyelesaikan tugasnya.

useCases.label: Action in Progress
useCases.example: Ibu sedang memasak rendang di dapur.

useCases.label: Anticipated Action
useCases.example: Kereta api akan berangkat pukul tujuh.

examples.en: Saya sudah membaca buku itu.
Adik belum tidur karena masih ramai.
Guru sedang menjelaskan materi baru.
Kami akan berlibur ke Bali besok.
Mereka belum pernah pergi ke luar negeri.

mistakes.note: Use 'belum' to express 'not yet' rather than combining 'sudah' with 'tidak'.
Aspect markers must precede the verb, never placed after it.
Do not stack aspect markers unnaturally; choose the primary aspect required.

quiz.question: To say 'I have already eaten', choose: Saya ___ makan.
quiz.explanation: 'Sudah' indicates completed or perfective aspect.

quiz.question: To express that someone has not arrived yet: Tamu itu ___ datang.
quiz.explanation: 'Belum' specifically expresses 'not yet'.

quiz.question: To say 'The teacher is currently talking': Guru ___ berbicara.
quiz.explanation: 'Sedang' marks continuous actions in progress.

quiz.question: To express a planned future trip: Kami ___ berangkat lusa.
quiz.explanation: 'Akan' functions as the prospective marker indicating future action.

tip: In conversational Indonesian, 'sudah' is frequently shortened to 'udah' and 'sedang' to 'lagi'.

title: Active Transitive Prefix meN-
subtitle: Forming active transitive verbs through nasalization rules
keyPoint: The prefix meN- derives active transitive verbs, dropping root-initial voiceless consonants K, P, T, and S into corresponding nasals.

cells: Velar and vowel bases take meng-

useCases.label: Voiceless Initial Deletion
useCases.example: Siti menyapu lantai kamar setiap pagi.

useCases.label: Voiced Initial Retention
useCases.example: Ayah membaca koran di teras rumah.

useCases.label: Vowel-Initial Attachment
useCases.example: Mereka mengambil foto pemandangan danau.

examples.en: Rina menulis surat untuk sahabatnya.
Kucing itu mengejar tikus kecil.
Budi meminjam buku sejarah di perpustakaan.
Polisi memeriksa dokumen pengemudi mobil.
Ibu memotong sayuran dengan pisau tajam.

mistakes.note: Root-initial 't' drops and nasalizes to 'n', resulting in 'menulis'.
Root-initial 'p' drops and nasalizes to 'm', forming 'memakai'.
Root-initial 's' turns into 'meny-', yielding 'menyapu'.

quiz.question: Select the correct meN- verb for root 'kirim':
quiz.explanation: Initial 'k' deletes and becomes nasal 'meng-', producing 'mengirim'.

quiz.question: Select the correct meN- verb for root 'tolong':
quiz.explanation: Initial 't' deletes and assimilates into 'menolong'.

quiz.question: Select the correct meN- verb for root 'beli':
quiz.explanation: Initial voiced 'b' is preserved after the bilabial nasal 'mem-'.

quiz.question: Select the correct meN- verb for root 'sapu':
quiz.explanation: Initial 's' drops and triggers 'meny-', producing 'menyapu'.

tip: Remember the mnemonic 'K-P-T-S': these four voiceless consonants always melt away into nasals when meN- is added.

title: Intransitive Prefix ber-
subtitle: Deriving intransitive, stative, reflexive, and possession verbs
keyPoint: The prefix ber- creates intransitive verbs that cannot take a direct object, often signaling states, possession, self-directed action, or reciprocity.

useCases.label: Motion and Activity
useCases.example: Anak-anak berlari di lapangan rumput.

useCases.label: Possession of State/Item
useCases.example: Paman memiliki toko dan beruang banyak.

useCases.label: Reciprocal / Social Action
useCases.example: Mereka berbicara tentang rencana liburan.

examples.en: Kami berenang di pantai setiap akhir pekan.
Ayah bekerja di kantor kementerian.
Mahasiswa berkumpul di aula kampus.
Dia bersepeda menuju stasiun kereta.
Mereka berjanji untuk saling menolong.

mistakes.note: 'Bekerja' is strictly intransitive; use transitive 'mengerjakan' before a direct object.
When the base starts with 'r', the prefix drops its 'r' and becomes 'be-'.

mistakes.wrong: Mereka berbelanja sayur itu di pasar.
mistakes.right: Mereka membeli sayur itu di pasar.
mistakes.note: 'Berbelanja' (intransitive shopping) cannot take a direct noun object; use 'membeli' to specify the bought object.

quiz.question: Form the correct ber- verb from the base 'ajar':
quiz.explanation: 'Ajar' is an irregular root that takes 'bel-', forming 'belajar'.

quiz.question: Which verb means 'to have/wear shoes'?
quiz.explanation: Affixing 'ber-' to the noun 'sepatu' yields 'to wear/have shoes'.

quiz.question: Form the correct ber- verb from the base 'kerja':
quiz.explanation: Roots containing '-er-' in the first syllable drop the 'r' of the prefix, giving 'bekerja'.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly uses an intransitive ber- verb?
quiz.explanation: Since 'berjalan' is intransitive, it connects to destinations via prepositions like 'ke'.

tip: A fast rule: if the verb has 'ber-', do not put a direct object noun right after it without a preposition.

title: Canonical Passive Prefix di-
subtitle: Passive constructions featuring third-person agents or unstated actors
keyPoint: Prefix di- attaches directly to the verb base to form passive clauses when the agent is a third person (dia, mereka, or a noun phrase).

cells: The book was read by Hasan.
The gate is locked every night.
The newspaper was bought by them.
The cake was eaten by little brother.

useCases.label: Third-Person Agent Mentioned
useCases.example: Mobil baru diperbaiki oleh montir berpengalaman.

useCases.label: Agent Omitted (Neutral)
useCases.example: Gedung pertemuan dibersihkan dua kali sehari.

useCases.label: Direct Post-Verbal Noun Agent
useCases.example: Tikus sawah dimakan burung hantu.

examples.en: Artikel ilmiah itu ditulis oleh Profesor Rudi.
Sepeda tua diperbaiki di bengkel kemarin.
Makanan tradisional disukai oleh para wisatawan.
Kopi panas diminum kakek di ruang tamu.
Lampu kamar dimatikan sebelum kami tidur.

mistakes.note: Type 1 passive with 'di-' is strictly forbidden with first-person agents; use Type 2 bare passive instead.
Passive prefix 'di-' must be attached to the root without a space, unlike the preposition 'di'.
Do not use 'di- ... oleh' for second-person agents in formal Indonesian; use bare passive 'kamu makan'.

quiz.question: Complete the passive sentence: Ikan bakar itu ___ oleh ayah.
quiz.explanation: The passive form with a 3rd person agent requires prefix 'di-', forming 'dimasak'.

quiz.question: Identify the incorrect passive construction:
quiz.explanation: 'Dimakan oleh saya' is grammatically unidiomatic; first-person agents require Type 2 passive 'saya makan'.

quiz.question: How should the passive verb for base 'tulis' be written?
quiz.explanation: Prefix 'di-' attaches directly to the verb base without spaces.

quiz.question: Which particle can introduce the agent after a di- verb?
quiz.explanation: 'Oleh' corresponds to 'by' in English agentive passive phrases.

tip: Spelling check: If it is a verb (action), attach 'di-' directly (dijual). If it is a location, put a space after 'di' (di toko).

title: Zero-Prefix Passive (Type 2)
subtitle: Passive constructions reserved for first and second person agents
keyPoint: When the agent is 1st or 2nd person (saya, aku, kami, kita, kamu, Anda), place the pronoun directly before the bare root verb without any prefix.

cells: This coffee has been made by me.
That book must be returned by you.
The major assignment will be discussed by us.
This question can be answered by you.

useCases.label: First-Person Singular (saya / ku-)
useCases.example: Kunci rumah sudah kuambil tadi pagi.

useCases.label: Second-Person Agent (kamu / Anda)
useCases.example: Baju batik ini harus kamu cuci dengan tangan.

useCases.label: Aspect/Modal Placement
useCases.example: Keputusan penting ini belum kami sepakati.

examples.en: Surat pernyataan ini sudah saya tandatangani.
Mobil tua itu akan kami jual minggu depan.
Dompet kulit itu sudah kauambil kemarin?
Pekerjaan rumah harus kalian selesaikan segera.
Buku cerita anak itu sudah kubaca tiga kali.

mistakes.note: In Type 2 passive, strip the 'meN-' prefix entirely; use the bare root base 'makan'.
Aspect markers and modals like 'sudah' must precede the pronoun agent, never split pronoun and verb.
Avoid using 3rd person passive 'di-... oleh' for first-person agents; use Type 2 'saya beli'.

quiz.question: Translate passively: 'The food has been eaten by me' -> Makanan itu sudah ___.
quiz.explanation: Type 2 passive combines the agent pronoun directly with the bare root: 'saya makan'.

quiz.question: Where should the modal 'harus' go in: 'Mobil itu ___ kamu cuci'?
quiz.explanation: Modals and aspect markers precede the pronoun-verb unit: 'harus kamu cuci'.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly reflects Type 2 passive word order?
quiz.explanation: Aspect marker (sudah) + Agent (saya) + Root (masak) is the strict order.

quiz.question: Using clitic 'ku-', complete: 'The letter was written by me' -> Surat itu ___.
quiz.explanation: The proclitic pronoun 'ku-' attaches directly to the bare root: 'kutulis'.

tip: Treat the pronoun and bare verb as an indivisible unit; never squeeze adverbs, negations, or modals between 'saya' and the verb root.

title: Relative Clauses and Nominalization with Yang
subtitle: Connecting descriptions, highlighting specific items, and saying 'the one which'
keyPoint: The word yang functions as a relative pronoun equivalent to who, which, or that, and turns adjectives into definite nouns like 'the red one'.

cells: It was he who came yesterday

useCases.label: Linking Descriptive Modifiers
useCases.example: Saya membeli buku yang tebal itu.

useCases.label: Nominalization ('The One')
useCases.example: Yang biru lebih murah daripada yang hijau.

useCases.label: Specifying People or Agents
useCases.example: Guru yang mengajar bahasa Indonesia sangat ramah.

examples.en: Saya mencari rumah yang memiliki halaman luas.
Kamu lebih suka kemeja yang mana?
Makanan yang dimasak ibu selalu enak.
Jangan ambil yang rusak itu.
Orang yang berdiri di dekat pintu adalah paman saya.

mistakes.note: The word 'yang' must precede the adjective or clause that modifies the noun, never stand at the end.
Do not insert 'yang' before basic possessive pronouns unless contrasting 'mine' as 'yang milik saya'.

mistakes.wrong: Dia orang siapa tinggal di sini.
mistakes.right: Dia orang yang tinggal di sini.
mistakes.note: Never use the question word 'siapa' as a relative pronoun; Indonesian uses 'yang' for both people and things.

quiz.question: Choose the correct phrase to complete: 'Saya mau beli baju ___ warna putih.'
quiz.explanation: 'Yang' is used to introduce the modifier specifying which shirt is being bought.

quiz.question: How do you say 'Which one is yours?' in Indonesian?
quiz.explanation: 'Yang mana' translates directly to 'which one'.

quiz.question: Complete the cleft sentence: 'Bukan saya, melainkan Budi ___ membawa kue itu.'
quiz.explanation: 'Yang' introduces the focalized agent who performed the action.

quiz.question: Identify the natural sentence meaning 'I prefer the hot one':
quiz.explanation: 'Yang panas' nominalizes the adjective 'panas' into 'the hot one'.

tip: Whenever you want to distinguish between options (e.g., 'the big one' vs 'the small one'), place 'yang' directly in front of the adjective: 'yang besar' and 'yang kecil'.

title: Discourse Particles (Sih, Dong, Kok, Deh, Kan)
subtitle: Adding nuance, emotion, and natural flow to conversational Indonesian
keyPoint: Indonesian discourse particles adjust the speaker's emotional stance, solidarity, or expectation without altering the basic propositional content.

useCases.label: Seeking Agreement or Confirming
useCases.example: Kamu sudah tahu berita itu, kan?

useCases.label: Expressing Surprise or Confusion
useCases.example: Kok kamu belum tidur jam begini?

useCases.label: Encouraging or Asserting Naturally
useCases.example: Bantu aku sebentar, dong!

examples.en: Dia kan sudah pernah ke Bali.
Kok lampunya tiba-tiba mati?
Boleh minta airnya sedikit, dong?
Sebenarnya sih saya tidak terlalu lapar.
Mending kita pulang sekarang saja, deh.

mistakes.note: 'Kok' appears at the beginning of the clause or predicate to express surprise, not tagged at the end like 'kan'.
'Dong' is placed immediately after the verb, request, or focal word, never as an opening sentence starter.

mistakes.right: Saya kan tidak tahu waktu itu, kan?
mistakes.note: Do not confuse the causal 'kan' (short for bukan/karena) with inappropriate formal usage; keep particles strictly in informal contexts.

quiz.question: Which particle best completes the friendly command: 'Ikut kita ke kafe, ___!'
quiz.explanation: 'Dong' softens an imperative into a warm, encouraging invitation ('come on, join us!').

quiz.question: Which particle conveys unexpected surprise in: '___ kamu bisa ada di sini?'
quiz.explanation: 'Kok' expresses mild bewilderment or curiosity ('How come you are here?').

quiz.question: Complete the tag question: 'Besok kita libur, ___?'
quiz.explanation: 'Kan' acts like 'right?' or 'isn't it?', appealing to common shared knowledge.

quiz.question: Express a mild personal concession: 'Kalau menurut saya ___, rencana ini bagus.'
quiz.explanation: 'Sih' serves as a pragmatic topic marker and conversational softener.

tip: Listen carefully to native speakers before overusing particles: 'kan' tags at the end or before predicates, 'kok' leads questions of surprise, and 'dong' softens requests.

title: Applicative Suffix -kan: Causative and Benefactive
subtitle: Causing an action or performing a deed for someone else's benefit
keyPoint: The verbal suffix -kan either causes an object to enter a state (causative) or shifts the beneficiary of an action into the primary direct object position (benefactive).

useCases.label: Causative Action (Cause to happen/become)
useCases.example: Ibu mematikan lampu kamar sebelum tidur.

useCases.label: Benefactive Action (Doing for someone)
useCases.example: Ayah membelikan adik sepeda baru.

useCases.label: Conveyance / Moving an Object
useCases.example: Dia melemparkan bola ke arah saya.

examples.en: Kakak membukakan pintu untuk tamunya.
Tolong dengarkan penjelasan guru dengan baik.
Polisi menghentikan mobil yang melanggar rambu.
Saya memasakkan teman saya nasi goreng.
Guru meminjamkan kamus kepada siswa.

mistakes.note: Without '-kan', the base verb 'membeli' cannot take the beneficiary directly after the verb without 'untuk'.
Causative verbs with '-kan' are strictly transitive and take their object directly without prepositions like 'dari' or 'pada'.

mistakes.wrong: Tolong buatkan kopi untuk kepada saya.
mistakes.note: When using the benefactive '-kan', the recipient directly follows the verb, making 'untuk kepada' redundant.

quiz.question: In 'Ibu membelikan adik baju', what role does 'adik' play?
quiz.explanation: The suffix '-kan' promotes the beneficiary ('adik') to the primary object position directly following the verb.

quiz.question: Which verb means 'to put something into' or 'insert'?
quiz.explanation: 'Memasukkan' is the causative form of 'masuk' (to enter), meaning to make something enter.

quiz.question: Complete the benefactive sentence: 'Bisa tolong ___ saya secangkir teh?'
quiz.explanation: 'Membuatkan' means to make something for someone (the speaker 'saya').

quiz.question: What is the causative form of 'bersih' (clean) meaning 'to clean something'?
quiz.explanation: 'Membersihkan' combines the meN- prefix and -kan suffix with root 'bersih' to mean 'to make clean'.

tip: Order matters with benefactive -kan: [Verb-kan] + [Person benefiting] + [Item]. For example: 'mengambilkan saya air' (get me water).

title: Locative and Iterative Suffix -i
subtitle: Targeting stationary locations, recipients, and repetitive actions
keyPoint: The suffix -i binds a stationary location or recipient directly to the verb as its object, or marks repetitive and iterative actions.

useCases.label: Stationary Target / Location
useCases.example: Presiden mengunjungi desa terpencil itu.

useCases.label: Recipient-Oriented Applicative
useCases.example: Paman mengirimi saya surat dari Jepang.

useCases.label: Iterative / Repeated Action
useCases.example: Petinju itu memukuli lawannya berkali-kali.

examples.en: Ratusan orang menghadiri seminar internasional tersebut.
Jangan mendekati binatang liar itu.
Polisi mencurigai pria berbaju hitam itu.
Ibu memarahi adik karena pulang terlambat.
Kami melewati jembatan tua setiap pagi.

mistakes.note: The suffix '-i' absorbs the preposition 'ke'; do not use prepositions between a '-i' verb and its locative object.
With 'mengirimi', the direct recipient immediately follows the verb; using 'kepada' is ungrammatical.

mistakes.wrong: Dia memasuki pensil ke dalam kotak.
mistakes.right: Dia memasukkan pensil ke dalam kotak.
mistakes.note: Use '-kan' when moving an object into something; use '-i' when the destination itself is the grammatical object (memasuki ruangan).

quiz.question: Complete with the correct locative verb: 'Rombongan turis ___ museum nasional.'
quiz.explanation: 'Memasuki' targets the location itself ('museum nasional') as the direct object.

quiz.question: What nuance does '-i' add to 'memukul' in 'Dia memukuli drum itu'?
quiz.explanation: The suffix '-i' denotes repeated, intense, or iterative action when attached to physical verbs like pukul (strike).

quiz.question: Choose the correct sentence following '-i' recipient grammar:
quiz.explanation: 'Mengirimi' requires the recipient ('saya') immediately following the verb without prepositions.

quiz.question: Complete the warning: 'Jangan ___ rel kereta api saat palang sudah turun!'
quiz.explanation: 'Mendekati' means to move toward or approach a physical stationary location or object.

tip: Contrast trick: -kan moves an item away towards a goal (memasukkan buku = put a book in), while -i stays fixed on the recipient/place (memasuki kamar = enter a room).

title: Adversative Verbs and Abstract Nouns with ke-...-an
subtitle: Expressing adverse victim experiences and creating abstract concepts
keyPoint: The circumfix ke-...-an derives either abstract nouns (qualities, states, domains) or involuntary adversative verbs where the subject suffers an unwanted mishap.

cells: Adversative Verb: caught in the rain

useCases.label: Adversative Experience (Unfortunate Event)
useCases.example: Tadi sore saya kehujanan di jalan.

useCases.label: Suffering a Loss or Deficit
useCases.example: Keluarga itu kehilangan rumah akibat kebakaran.

useCases.label: Abstract Noun Formation
useCases.example: Kesehatan jauh lebih berharga daripada uang.

examples.en: Mereka kelaparan karena bantuan belum tiba.
Keamanan lingkungan ini selalu terjaga dengan baik.
Saya kemalaman dan tidak ada angkutan umum lagi.
Ketinggian gunung itu mencapai tiga ribu meter.
Banyak warga kepanasan di tengah lapangan terbuka.

mistakes.note: 'Menghujani' means to shower something with objects, while 'kehujanan' conveys the accidental experience of getting caught in the rain.
Use 'kehilangan' (loss) derived from 'hilang', not unrelated base roots when describing accidental losses.

mistakes.wrong: Adil adalah penting bagi semua orang.
mistakes.right: Keadilan adalah hal penting bagi semua orang.
mistakes.note: 'Adil' is an adjective ('just/fair'); the abstract noun 'justice' requires the circumfix 'ke-...-an' to become 'keadilan'.

quiz.question: Which word derived from 'malam' (night) means 'to be overtaken by nightfall'?
quiz.explanation: 'Kemalaman' is an adversative ke-...-an verb meaning caught by nightfall or stranded late.

quiz.question: Convert the adjective 'bersih' (clean) into the abstract noun 'cleanliness':
quiz.explanation: The circumfix ke-...-an forms abstract quality nouns from adjectives: 'bersih' becomes 'kebersihan'.

quiz.question: In 'Dia kehilangan kunci motornya', what does 'kehilangan' indicate?
quiz.explanation: Adversative ke-...-an verbs highlight that the subject unintentionally suffered an unwanted experience or loss.

quiz.question: Select the correct word to fill the blank: '___ udara di kota ini semakin buruk.'
quiz.explanation: 'Pencemaran' (pollution) represents the nominalized process affecting air quality in the sentence.

tip: When an adverse verb has ke-...-an, think of it as 'undergoing too much of' or 'being struck by' the root word: hujan -> kehujanan (trapped in rain), dingin -> kedinginan (suffering from cold).

title: Nominalization: peN-, peN-...-an, and -an
subtitle: Form agents, ongoing processes, and concrete results from base words
keyPoint: Prefix peN- derives the agent or instrument, circumfix peN-...-an marks the abstract process or action, while suffix -an indicates the concrete result or product.

useCases.label: Agent / Instrument (peN-)
useCases.example: Pemerintah mencari penerjemah resmi untuk konferensi internasional.

useCases.label: Process or Action (peN-...-an)
useCases.example: Proses pembuatan dokumen ini membutuhkan waktu dua minggu.

useCases.label: Result or Object (-an)
useCases.example: Masakan ibu selalu menjadi makanan favorit seluruh keluarga.

examples.en: Penulis artikel itu memenangkan penghargaan bergengsi.
Penulisan laporan keuangan harus selesai sebelum akhir bulan.
Tulisan tangannya sangat rapi dan mudah dibaca oleh dosen.
Pengembangan sektor pariwisata meningkatkan devisa negara secara signifikan.
Bantuan kemanusiaan telah tiba di lokasi bencana alam pagi ini.

mistakes.wrong: Proses menulis buku itu makan waktu setahun.
mistakes.right: Proses penulisan buku itu memakan waktu setahun.
mistakes.note: Use the derived nominal circumfix peN-...-an (penulisan) rather than the active verb base after 'proses'.
The suffix -an is required to change the verbal action 'masak' into the concrete noun 'masakan' (cooked dish/food).

mistakes.wrong: Pembersihan itu bekerja dengan sangat teliti setiap pagi.
mistakes.right: Pembersih itu bekerja dengan sangat teliti setiap pagi.
mistakes.note: Use peN- (pembersih) for the agent or tool; peN-...-an (pembersihan) designates the abstract act of cleaning.

quiz.question: Para dokter mengawasi ___ pasien secara intensif di ruang gawat darurat.
quiz.explanation: Circumfix peN-...-an is needed to denote the medical process or examination.

quiz.question: Dia dikenal sebagai seorang novelis dan ___ puisi terkenal di kota ini.
quiz.explanation: The prefix peN- forms the human agent (pembaca = reader/reciter).

quiz.question: Kami membaca banyak ___ klasik selama liburan musim panas.
quiz.explanation: Suffix -an produces the concrete object/material being read (bacaan = reading material/literature).

quiz.question: Kementerian Keuangan mengumumkan rencana ___ jembatan antarprovinsi.
quiz.explanation: Pembangunan expresses the ongoing process or project of development/construction.

tip: Match the nasal morphophonemics of peN- and peN-...-an directly to meN-: if the verb is menulis, the derived nouns are penulis and penulisan.

title: Reduplication Types and Functions
subtitle: Master full, partial, and sound-altering repetition in Indonesian
keyPoint: Indonesian reduplication alters word meaning systematically, indicating noun pluralization, repetitive or relaxed verbal activity, mutual reciprocity, or intensified qualities.

useCases.label: Plurality & Diversity
useCases.example: Buku-buku di perpustakaan nasional tersusun rapi menurut kategori ilmiah.

useCases.label: Casual / Relaxed Action
useCases.example: Kami hanya duduk-duduk di teras rumah sambil menikmati secangkir kopi panas.

useCases.label: Reciprocal / Mutual Interaction
useCases.example: Kedua belah pihak saling tolong-menolong dalam mengatasi krisis pangan ini.

examples.en: Guru meminta semua murid-murid kembali ke dalam kelas masing-masing.
Pada akhir pekan, keluarga kami sering jalan-jalan ke taman kota.
Mereka bersalaman dan saling maaf-memaafkan di hari raya yang fitri.
Bus antarkota itu mondar-mandir menjemput penumpang di sepanjang jalan raya.
Mobil-mobilan kayu ini dibuat sendiri oleh paman dengan ketelitian tinggi.

mistakes.note: Avoid double pluralization: do not reduplicate the noun if a quantifier like 'banyak' or 'semua' is already present.

mistakes.right: Mereka pukul-memukul saat pertengkaran itu terjadi.
mistakes.note: Use the reciprocal reduplication template stem + meN-stem (pukul-memukul) to convey mutual interaction.

mistakes.wrong: Kami mau jalan di taman santai.
mistakes.right: Kami mau jalan-jalan santai di taman.
mistakes.note: Reduplicating intransitive dynamic verbs like jalan to jalan-jalan expresses aimless leisure rather than purposeful transit.

quiz.question: Setelah pertengkaran panjang, kedua sahabat itu akhirnya saling ___.
quiz.explanation: The pattern base + meN-base (maaf-memaafkan) conveys mutual, reciprocal action.

quiz.question: Budi suka menghabiskan sore hari dengan ___ di tepi pantai.
quiz.explanation: Full reduplication of the verb stem (duduk-duduk) communicates relaxed, leisurely activity.

quiz.question: Di supermarket itu, terdapat aneka ___ segar yang diimpor dari luar negeri.
quiz.explanation: Reduplication with the suffix -an (buah-buahan) creates a collective noun meaning 'various sorts of fruits'.

quiz.question: Jangan menumpuk terlalu banyak ___ referensi di atas meja belajar.
quiz.explanation: 'Banyak' already establishes plurality, so the singular root 'buku' must be used without reduplication.

tip: Reduplication plus the suffix -an (e.g., mobil-mobilan, rumah-rumahan) creates diminutive or imitation nouns meaning 'toy car' or 'model house'.

title: Prefix ter-: Involuntary Actions and Superlatives
subtitle: Express accidental outcomes, completed states, potential, and extremes
keyPoint: The prefix ter- marks non-volitional involuntary events, non-agentive resulting states, ability in negative frames, and absolute superlatives when bound to adjectives.

useCases.label: Accidental / Unintentional Event
useCases.example: Kaki kucing malang itu tidak sengaja terinjak oleh saya ketika berjalan.

useCases.label: Static Resultant State
useCases.example: Pintu gerbang museum selalu terbuka lebar bagi pengunjung dari berbagai daerah.

useCases.label: Absolute Superlative
useCases.example: Gedung pencakar langit ini dinobatkan sebagai bangunan tertinggi di ibu kota.

examples.en: Gelas antik peninggalan kakek terjatuh dari meja dan pecah berantakan.
Buku catatan harian saya tertinggal di dalam gerbong kereta listrik tadi pagi.
Kotak brankas yang berat itu tidak terangkat oleh dua orang pekerja sekalipun.
Mahasiswa itu mencatatkan namanya sebagai lulusan terbaik di fakultas hukum.
Jendela kamar tidur masih terkunci rapat saat pencuri mencoba masuk ke dalam.

mistakes.wrong: Saya sengaja tertabrak tiang listrik kemarin sore.
mistakes.right: Saya menabrak tiang listrik kemarin sore.
mistakes.note: Prefix ter- implies unintentional or accidental events; deliberate intentional actions must use meN-.

mistakes.wrong: Kue itu termakan oleh saya karena saya sangat lapar.
mistakes.right: Kue itu saya makan karena saya sangat lapar.
mistakes.note: Use standard canonical passive (di- or object pronoun + root) when the consumption was voluntary and intentional.

mistakes.wrong: Gedung itu paling tertinggi di Asia Tenggara.
mistakes.right: Gedung itu tertinggi di Asia Tenggara.
mistakes.note: 'Ter-' on an adjective already means 'the most'. Do not combine it redundantly with 'paling'.

quiz.question: Maafkan saya, berkas rahasia perusahaan tidak sengaja ___ kemarin siang.
quiz.explanation: Prefix ter- marks involuntary or accidental actions ('accidentally thrown away').

quiz.question: Batu besar yang menghalangi jalan pegunungan itu tidak ___ oleh warga desa.
quiz.explanation: In negative contexts (tidak + ter-), ter- denotes involuntary potentiality or capability ('cannot be shifted').

quiz.question: Gunung Kerinci merupakan gunung berapi ___ di kepulauan Indonesia.
quiz.explanation: Prefix ter- attached to an adjective creates the absolute superlative form ('highest').

quiz.question: Saat kami tiba di gedung pertemuan, pintu aula utama sudah ___ lebar.
quiz.explanation: Terbuka represents a passive static resultant state ('in an open state').

tip: Never combine 'paling' with a 'ter-' adjective (avoid *paling terbagus*). Either write 'paling bagus' or 'terbagus' independently.

title: Complex Causatives: memper-, memper-...-kan, memper-...-i
subtitle: Express intensified causation, acquisition, comparison, and reformative actions
keyPoint: The prefix memper- makes adjectives comparative or causative, while adding suffixes -kan or -i produces complex multi-tiered transitive verbs signifying treatment, acquisition, or repetitive spatial causation.

useCases.label: Causative from Adjectives (memper-)
useCases.example: Pemerintah kota memperlebar jalan protokol guna mengurai kemacetan parah.

useCases.label: Causative with Recipient (memper-...-kan)
useCases.example: Direktur utama memperkenalkan kepala divisi logistik yang baru kepada staf.

useCases.label: Iterative / Renewal (memper-...-i)
useCases.example: Perusahaan wajib memperbarui izin operasional pabrik setiap lima tahun sekali.

examples.en: Ilmuwan berusaha mempercepat proses uji klinis obat antiviral generasi baru.
Dosen tamu itu memperlihatkan dokumen sejarah kuno di depan seluruh mahasiswa.
Raja akhirnya mempersunting putri bangsawan dari kerajaan tetangga setelah perang.
Pihak kontraktor sedang memperbaiki instalasi listrik yang rusak akibat korsleting.
Pengacara itu berusaha memperjelas keterangan saksi kunci di hadapan majelis hakim.

mistakes.note: Do not attach the suffix -kan to memper- when the base is an adjective; use simple 'memperbesar' (or 'membesarkan'), never *memperbesarkan*.

mistakes.right: Dia mempertemukan kedua temannya di kafe.
mistakes.note: The circumfix memper-...-kan is mandatory when applying a transitive causative action to a verb root like 'temu'.
The standard Baku Indonesian base is 'baru', giving the derived form 'memperbarui' without intrusive historical 'h'.

quiz.question: Arsitek itu mendesain ulang ruangan ini untuk ___ kapasitas ruang pertemuan.
quiz.explanation: With adjective roots like luas, memper- alone signifies 'to make more [adjective]'. Suffix -kan is redundant and ungrammatical here.

quiz.question: Duta besar Indonesia berniat ___ delegasi diplomatik kepada presiden.
quiz.explanation: The causative verb 'to introduce' requires the circumfix memper-...-kan on the base root kenal.

quiz.question: Teknisi handal itu segera ___ jaringan internet kantor yang terputus mendadak.
quiz.explanation: The standard verb meaning 'to repair/fix' uses the circumfix memper-...-i (memperbaiki).

quiz.question: Latihan pernapasan secara rutin terbukti ampuh untuk ___ daya tahan tubuh.
quiz.explanation: Adjectives take simple prefix memper- to form causatives (memperkuat = to strengthen).

tip: Remember the golden constraint: Adjective + memper- never takes -kan. Choose either 'memperdalam' OR 'mendalamkan', never *memperdalamkan*.

title: Formal vs Informal Register Shifts
subtitle: Convert between Bahasa Baku and colloquial Indonesian grammar
keyPoint: Informal Indonesian systematically drops verbal nasal prefixes, substitutes the causative/applicative suffixes -kan and -i with -in, and replaces formal vocabulary with colloquial particles and pronouns.

useCases.label: Dropped Active Nasal Prefix
useCases.example: Kamu mau beli kopi di warung seberang jalan nggak?

useCases.label: Suffix -in for -kan / -i
useCases.example: Tolong bersihin meja makan ini sebelum tamu-tamu datang berkunjung.

useCases.label: Colloquial Lexicon & Particles
useCases.example: Gue udah bilang sama dia kemarin, tapi dia tetep aja lupa.

examples.en: Kemarin gue udah selesai ngerjain tugas kuliah sampai larut malam.
Tolong bukain pintu depan dong, tangan gue lagi penuh barang belanjaan.
Mereka nggak mau ngomong langsung sama kepala cabang bank itu.
Jangan dipikirin terus masalah sepele kayak gitu, bikin stres aja.
Lo mau ikut nonton konser musik jazz bareng anak-anak nanti malam?

mistakes.wrong: Dalam surat dinas resmi, direktur nulis pengumuman baru.
mistakes.right: Dalam surat dinas resmi, direktur menulis pengumuman baru.
mistakes.note: Prefix-dropping and colloquial variants like 'nulis' are strictly prohibited in formal or institutional correspondence.

mistakes.wrong: Gue ingin mengajukan permohonan beasiswa kepada Anda.
mistakes.right: Saya ingin mengajukan permohonan beasiswa kepada Bapak/Ibu.
mistakes.note: Do not mix ultra-informal pronouns (gue) with formal institutional verb forms and polite requests.

mistakes.wrong: Dosen meminta mahasiswa kumpulin skripsi tepat waktu.
mistakes.right: Dosen meminta mahasiswa mengumpulkan skripsi tepat waktu.
mistakes.note: In academic and official settings, use the canonical circumfix meng-...-kan instead of the colloquial suffix -in.

quiz.question: Buku laporan pertanggungjawaban itu harus segera ___ kepada atasan.
quiz.explanation: In formal standard register (Bahasa Baku), passive verbs retain the canonical di-...-kan affixation ('diberikan').

quiz.question: Eh, lo udah ___ adik lo hadiah ulang tahun belum?
quiz.explanation: In informal conversational Indonesian, the applicative suffix -kan is replaced by -in ('beliin').

quiz.question: Saya mohon izin untuk tidak menghadiri rapat karena ___ enak badan.
quiz.explanation: 'Kurang enak badan' is the idiomatic standard expression; 'nggak' and 'kagak' are inappropriate in formal letters.

quiz.question: Tolong matiin lampu kamar sebelum tidur. Bentuk baku dari 'matiin' adalah ___.
quiz.explanation: The informal root + -in in an imperative maps directly to the active transitive stem meN-...-kan ('mematikan') in formal register.

tip: Colloquial verbs starting with vowels or velar sounds often take 'ng-' (e.g., ngomong, ngambil, ngatur), which transforms into 'meng-' in standard written Indonesian.
